newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss pays world record price for Cuban cigars.
newsitem.headline: Swiss pays world record price for Cuban cigars.

text.p: A Swiss buyer paid 16,100 Swiss francs ($11,431) for a box of 25 Cuban cigars rarely available commercially, tripling the pre-sale estimate and setting a record price for a cigar at auction, Christie's said on Tuesday.

The 25 "Trinidad" cigars, 19 cm (7.5 inches) long each and packed in their original cedar box, were from the special selection of the Cuban national factory generally reserved for diplomats and other dignitaries, it added.

"Rarely available commercially, particularly in boxes of 25 of which only two are known to exist, this is the first time they have ever been offered at auction," Christie's said in a statement on the sale, held in Geneva on Sunday evening.
"These cigars are made specially for the (Cuban) government and are offered from time to time to heads of state and other important visitors," a Christie's spokeswoman told Reuters.

Christie's said the new price of 644 Swiss francs ($450) per cigar set a record for a cigar at auction, surpassing the previous mark of 214 francs per unit ($140) achieved at Christie's in London in 1996 for 163 cigars belonging to the Duke of Buccleuch.
The Swiss who bid by telephone for the 1996 Trinidad cigars (ring gauge 38) asked to remain anonymous, according to the spokeswoman. Neither was the name of the seller disclosed.
